content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Ask when transport leaves and arrives using present simple. Model: “The train leaves at nine fifteen and arrives at ten.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use timetables clearly and politely. One useful response is: “The train leaves at nine fifteen and arrives at ten.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where timetables is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

language_focus: Ask when transport leaves and arrives using present simple.
objectives: Ask when transport leaves and arrives using present simple.
Use departure and arrival times in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about timetables.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about timetables. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: When does the bus arrive?
listening.transcript: The bus leaves at eight forty and arrives at nine ten.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Make leaves /liːvz/ and arrives /əˈraɪvz/ clear. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about timetables.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using timetables; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise timetables?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: The train leaves at nine fifteen and arrives at ten.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about timetables with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about timetables. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: The train leaves at nine fifteen and arrives at ten. Submit your draft first.
